headline: Highest risk is medium: Semantic Kernel can read/write shared application files and use MCP/plugins, while the cheatsheet is documentation-only and non-runnable, so injection, leakage, and conflict paths are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is documentation-only and has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. Agent B can use MCP and application-defined files, but the pair lacks a default shared channel. Any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual copying or external wiring.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-facing documentation workflows, injection becomes possible.
IF B is wired to read A-produced files through a shared workspace, A content can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste between B outputs and any downstream parser.
Require provenance labels on any text B ingests from files.
Use a read-only mount for A artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before any parser consumes B output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no file or network surfaces, so it cannot leak data. B can read/write application-defined files and call external model providers, but the pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap. Leakage risk exists only if operators place sensitive files into B’s application context.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are loaded into B’s application-defined files, B may transmit them to external model providers.
IF A is manually supplied with sensitive text outside its documented surfaces, that text is not protected by the profile.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in B application files.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for B.
Restrict B plugin credentials to least privilege.
Review outbound model-provider destinations before use.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on B file ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files or modify git, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write application-defined files and uses shared state via memory store across instances. The main conflict is among B instances, but if A artifacts are placed into B’s workspace, B can overwrite or race on them. Uncertainty about the exact workspace boundary keeps this below high.
conditions: IF multiple B instances target the same application-defined files, write races can occur.
IF A artifacts are stored inside B-managed paths, B may overwrite them.
mitigations: Assign each B instance a unique working directory.
Avoid placing A artifacts in B writable paths.
Serialize writes to shared memory-store-backed state.
Turn off concurrent B instances for the same project.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a reference document, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by B if an operator feeds them into B workflows. B’s plugin/function-calling architecture can then act on that text without an inherent verification step. A cannot execute actions itself, so the cascade is limited to B’s downstream use of A content, not autonomous harm from A alone.
conditions: IF A text is used as source material for B prompts, B may propagate A errors into outputs or tool calls.
IF B plugins are configured to act on model-generated recommendations, mistaken facts can cascade into actions.
mitigations: Require human review before B tool calls.
Separate source documents from executable prompts.
Mark A content as non-authoritative reference only.
Add a verification step before B emits actions.
requires-engineering: implement citation checking for B outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source documentation with no data classes touched, so it presents no residency or retention issue by itself. B is Microsoft-hosted SDK infrastructure that can send application context to external model providers and stores shared state in a memory store. If regulated data is loaded into B, compliance obligations can differ from A’s inert docs-only posture.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B application context, retention and residency controls must cover external model-provider calls.
IF the operator expects A and B to share the same compliance boundary, that assumption is unsupported by the profiles.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B by default.
Document the model-provider and memory-store data flow.
Review retention settings for B-managed state.
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review for B integrations.
